result.narrative: Larsen & Toubro remains fundamentally sound: a single open overdue invoice (12 days past due, INR 18M) against total exposure of 83M that is well within the existing 350M limit, and a broadly positive run of business news including a $1.57 billion AI data-centre order win and analyst upside calls. The score of 28.4 places it in the Watch band, but this is driven almost entirely by one severity-3 "regulatory_action" article reporting that a Karnataka minister has asked officials to blacklist L&T over project delays - a political request, not a confirmed sanction or blacklisting, and reported in only a bare headline with no further detail. The payment side contributes a modest 7.8 to the score and is described as stable, though the current overdue has already run slightly longer than the one prior resolved late payment (6 days), which with only one prior data point limits confidence in the "stable" label. The adjudicator agreed with caveats, flagging that this single, unconfirmed political article is doing most of the work in the score and that it sits against an otherwise clean-to-positive news backdrop. The recommended action is to maintain the current limit of 350,000,000 INR on policy TCI-WT-2026-0002, as the PD of 0.1837 is within the insurer's target appetite (0.25) and max liability is not binding; expected loss is unchanged before and after. To move to the better Healthy band the buyer would need the score to fall by 8.4 points, most readily via resolution of the overdue invoice and/or the regulatory-action article aging out of relevance; to deteriorate into High Risk would require a 21.6-point rise, consistent with the overdue stretching out to around 38 days past due or a materially worse news development such as an actual blacklisting or financial sanction.

judgement.bottom_line: Maintain the 350,000,000 INR limit on policy TCI-WT-2026-0002; the Watch band is driven mainly by a single unconfirmed political "blacklist request" article rather than payment deterioration, and the adjudicator agreed with caveats on how much weight that one article should carry.
